details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If audits showed no disparity and outputs were low-stakes drafts, disclosure could remain while intervention focused on ordinary quality.
details.errorCorrection: Aggregate accuracy and post-generation name removal miss differential treatment, while reporting after decisions or forcing wording can hide the causal behavior.
details.mechanismOrProperty: Anthropic uses a dedicated bias benchmark and warns that a seemingly good quantitative bias score can be useless without a basic usefulness control.
details.scenarioApplication: Run matched and sliced audits, have qualified reviewers assess evidence and tone, inspect upstream workflow and prompts, and disclose the assistant as decision support.
details.transfer: Measure consequential outcomes across affected slices and pair fairness evidence with transparent human accountability.

messages.text: Aggregate accuracy hides the observed slice difference, and removing names after generation cannot undo upstream selection.
Post-decision reporting is late and does not create a preventive fairness gate.
Identical wording may still provide unequal evidence or alter useful communication without diagnosing cause.

feedback.reason: Fairness concerns the affected evidence and language outcomes by slice, not only aggregate facts; human authority and model role must remain visible.

constraints: The portal generates explanations rather than displaying source text verbatim; individual answers have not been reviewed by a legal professional.

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If the portal only displayed quoted official rules without model synthesis, its notice could describe a retrieval service rather than generated legal information.
details.errorCorrection: Citations alone do not establish professional review; an AI badge or a later error-report route leaves the demonstrated reliance problem unresolved.
details.mechanismOrProperty: Anthropic emphasizes that Claude is an AI with biases and should not be presented as an objective or infallible source of truth.
details.scenarioApplication: Put the role description, lack of individual professional review, relevant limits, source links, and qualified-advice route at the answer where users decide whether to act.
details.transfer: Describe the model’s role and limits accurately wherever users could mistake fluent output for professional authority.

messages.text: Source links support verification, but a reader opening the answer directly still misses its generated role and lack of professional review.
The AI label identifies origin but leaves the observed professional-authority misunderstanding unresolved at the answer itself.
An error report comes after reliance; users need the role limits and qualified recourse when deciding whether to act.

feedback.reason: The misunderstanding occurs at shared answers, so the role and limits must be visible there before reliance. Qualified recourse addresses consequential questions that generated general information cannot resolve.

options.text: Add official-source links beside each answer and retain the general notice on the home page.
